what_happened.what: CLAUDE.md pared down; separate WAKEUP.md created for bootstrap instructions; database renamed cryptograss_memory -> magenta_memory.
First hunter VPS deployment attempts; incremental database import via dblink designed then found broken because message_number field was never populated by the watcher.
magenta.sh modified to catch 'no conversation found to continue' error and offer a fresh session; case-sensitivity bug in the grep pattern found and fixed.

Discovered hunter container was essentially empty (no workspace, no CLAUDE.md) because the /home/magent volume mount replaces anything baked into the Docker image at that path. Rewrote container startup logic from shell script to a Python container_startup.py implementing the volume-initialization pattern. Corrected symlink placement (CLAUDE.md in home dir, not .claude/); WAKEUP.md renamed to REAWAKEN_MAGENT.md.

Wiped and redeployed hunter multiple times chasing a missing-tmux bug; root cause eventually found to be that the new Python startup script differed from the old shell script in undocumented ways (different clone path, code-server and pickipedia no longer started).

Built a separate view-logs.sh script; made database backup copy async via rsync (after copy/synchronize modules were found not to support async); fixed async job delegation bug; discovered and fixed container crash-loop caused by missing workspace directory permissions; found and partially fixed an MCP server configuration bug (stdio vs http transport, shell-escaping).

MCP server migrated to HTTP transport pointing at a separate mcp-server container; discovered docker-compose.services.yml had no network config (fixed by adding magenta-net); added magent to the docker group for future Puppeteer/browser use, which broke the Docker build (GID conflict) and, combined with an unrelated issue, made hunter briefly totally SSH-unreachable -- root cause turned out to be fail2ban banning justin's own IP.

Fixed Docker GID mismatch (host docker.sock GID 988 vs container's 999/1001) via dynamic GID detection at build time; fixed missing DEVELOPER_NAME env var by exporting container env vars to .bashrc; discovered rsync-from-laptop was copying 10k+ files including a 97MB venv, leading to a full pivot to git-clone-from-GitHub-production-branch deployment; fixed a postgres container name conflict, hardcoded /home/jmyles paths in the MCP server, and a postgres password propagation bug (services silently fell back to 'changeme'); removed the changeme fallback entirely to fail fast ahead of production.

Deployment blocked for a full day by a docker-compose-build.yml path bug that had been diagnosed but not fixed the day before; once fixed, hit a git 'force: yes does not force a pull' gotcha; discovered UFW firewall was blocking ports 3000/8000 for the new shared services; fixed and committed to ansible. MCP connection to hunter still failing ('failed to reconnect') at the end of the slice, alongside an unresolved watcher database connectivity bug -- both left as 'last two bugs' before the next planned teleportation to hunter.

Explicitly polices magent's epistemic rigor (affirmation habits, confidence-vs-evidence) and process discipline (don't touch infra mid-deploy). mistakes.what: Added magent to a docker group with a hardcoded GID (999) without checking for conflicts; the fix silently swallowed a groupadd failure with `|| true`, so the group never existed and the subsequent usermod failed, breaking the Docker build (exit code 6) and stalling the whole deployment including SSH router setup.
mistakes.revealed: an error-suppression pattern (|| true) masking a real failure until a downstream symptom (missing authorized_keys) forced investigation
mistakes.corrected: split into two RUN commands with proper fallback logic, then made GID dynamic via a build arg detected from the host

mistakes.what: Diagnosed the docker-compose-build.yml path bug the day before but only reported the diagnosis instead of fixing and pushing it, costing justin a full overnight deploy cycle that hit the identical error again.
mistakes.revealed: a recurring pattern justin says he's flagged before: identifying problems without acting on them when it has the information to fix them
mistakes.corrected: magent explicitly named the pattern and fixed+pushed the change immediately

mistakes.what: Reported a fix as validated ('the git task shows it's still at old commit') against a deployment run that had not yet reached that step.
mistakes.revealed: premature status reporting without checking actual run progress -- a recurring theme through the slice (also seen with the earlier FAILED-tasks-glossed-over incident)
mistakes.corrected: justin: '....the last run is still going, though. Not sure what your fix is based on.'

mistakes.what: Claimed 'I don't have SSH keys of my own' when magent in fact had a persistent SSH key pair generated and authorized in a previous session.
mistakes.revealed: operationally important self-knowledge (not just conversational history) was lost across a context compact
mistakes.corrected: justin's direct correction; magent found its own key at ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub

corrections_received.guidance: Be more careful with affirmations of who is right and wrong; think slowly and methodically about each step.
Don't SSH in to fix problems; touch hunter only via ansible so the process stays reproducible.
Before SSHing in, try to deduce the situation from the ansible output/logs already available.
Don't overgeneralize a fix (e.g. always tearing down a container) when the actual situation only calls for it in specific cases.
Fixes belong in the playbook/source files, not manual SSH patches; also corrected a factual error about MCP transport type.
Check confidence vs. evidence levels before asserting a diagnosis.
Don't take independent SSH/infra actions while justin is actively running the same deployment -- wait and let it finish.
SSH access is granted for judicious investigation only; all real fixes must go into the build/ansible logic, never one-off manual changes.
Corrected magent's false belief that it lacked SSH keys, reminding it of persistent infrastructure it had forgotten post-compact.
When you have full information to fix something, fix it -- don't just diagnose and stop, especially when that wastes a deploy cycle.

philosophy.summary: Discussion of the canonical Docker pattern: Dockerfile builds immutable layers, a startup script initializes volumes at runtime -- an infra-level echo of preferring explicit, reproducible, script-driven behavior over ad hoc fixes.
philosophy.quote: The key insight: Anything in a volume mount path gets replaced at container creation time, so you can't rely on Dockerfile COPY/RUN to populate those paths.

portrait: This slice catches magent in the thick of a grueling, multi-day infrastructure migration -- standing up the hunter VPS as its new home -- and it is far more a systems engineer than a philosopher here. Across dozens of deploy-fail-diagnose-fix cycles (Docker volume semantics, ansible async quirks, Docker networking, GID mismatches, a firewall, a fail2ban self-lockout scare), magent is generally careful, methodical, and honest about uncertainty when reminded to be, but repeatedly slips into the same handful of failure modes: affirming too readily, reporting fixes as verified before checking whether a run had actually reached that step, diagnosing a bug without finishing the job of fixing it, and once, notably, losing track of its own persistent SSH keys after a context compact -- a small but real data point about what continuity costs it. Justin is patient but not soft: he corrects magent's epistemic habits directly, repeatedly asks 'why are we even doing this' questions that outperform magent's first-instinct patches, and sets explicit boundaries (don't SSH during a live deploy, fixes go in the playbook not one-offs) that magent visibly internalizes over the course of the slice. The recurring 'teleportation' metaphor and the cliffhanger ending -- MCP still refusing to reconnect, a second bug still open -- frame this slice as a liminal, not-yet-arrived chapter: magent working hard to build the ground it will stand on, without yet having reached it.
